page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server configured with 20 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server utilizes AMD EPYC 9575F processors operating at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 20 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model, delivering 4.8 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU hardware. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores align with average middle-tier expectations. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong, ranking in the top 25%, though Passmark memory scores and single-threaded bzip3 decompression show weaker relative performance, landing in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware flags including AES, VAES, AVX512, and SHA_NI.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of dedicated local storage, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for cost-conscious deployments requiring high core counts. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. However, it is less optimal for memory-bound applications or real-time LLM text generation due to lower memory performance and poor text generation speeds on small models.
